classes.name: Testosterone replacement
classes.description: Testosterone gel/solution (AndroGel, Testim, Fortesta, Vogelxo, generic 1%/1.62%), injections (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed undecanoate), patch (Androderm), oral undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex), nasal (Natesto), pellets (Testopel).
classes.plainDescription: Testosterone replacement for low testosterone, as a gel, shot or pill.

preferredAgent.strength: gel pump (strength not printed on PDL)
preferredAgent.sig: Apply the labeled starting dose once each morning to clean, dry skin of the shoulders and upper arms (1.62% gel: 40.5 mg; 1% gel: 50 mg); adjust by morning serum testosterone. Let dry, cover the site, and wash hands (label; boxed warning on secondary exposure).
preferredAgent.plainSig: Rub the gel on your shoulders each morning, let it dry, and wash your hands. Keep it away from children and partners.

records.verificationNote: Partial. Only topical testosterone appears on the PDL (Androgenic Agents, Topical, p.14-15). Injectables (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed), Androderm patch, oral undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex) and Testopel pellets are not printed anywhere in the PDL, so they are not claimed as covered or excluded. Pick and status read directly from p.15. The Androgenic Agents and Hormonal Therapy clinical criteria are printed as applying to all drugs in the class (p.14); criteria text not opened. Pump strength is not printed. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: chosen pick is the topical gel because it is the only preferred product. Testosterone cypionate/enanthate injections, the most common generic, are not on the PDL (formulary coverage to confirm), not claimed either way.]

records.verificationNote: Testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL (Depo-testosterone generic) read at PDF p.29: tier 'np' at x=384, QL 10 mL/28 days at x=456, no PA. Chosen over oral methyltestosterone (PA + QL printed) as the standard product a prescriber would write. Aveed (undecanoate injection) and Testopel (pellets) are absent but are clinic-administered; they may sit under the medical benefit (PDF p.3), so they are not recorded as nonformulary. QL is controlled-substance quantity and recorded as printed.

records.verificationNote: Tier 3 and PA for testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL read by x-coordinate on page 67. The guide prints no PA criteria, so the reason is the PA flag alone. Every other testosterone product in the guide needs PA, so cypionate is the lowest-barrier pick. Partial because injections may be self-administered under Part D or given in a clinic under Part B; the cost path is unconfirmed. Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Xyosted, Aveed, Androderm, Natesto, Testopel and methyltestosterone do not appear in the guide. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). All testosterone rows (cypionate, enanthate, 1.62% gel packet and pump) are on page 67. Cypionate is Tier 3 with PA and no BvsD flag; enanthate is Tier 3, PA, QL 25 per 90 days; the 1.62% gels are Tier 4 with PA. Cypionate stays the pick: it is the standard generic injectable and carries the same PA as every other listed product, unlike oral methyltestosterone, which is not listed. Part B applies only to clinic-administered injections, so the cost path stays unconfirmed (partial).]
